name: Darce Choke from Side Control
description: Learn the D'Arce head-and-arm choke from Side Control, including the rolling Marce finish, early defenses, and progressive partner practice.
target_area: Sides of the neck, with the trapped shoulder completing the head-and-arm choke
summary: The D'Arce Choke from Side Control traps the opponent's arm beside their neck with an under-armpit thread and figure-four grip; the named Marce variation finishes by rolling onto the shoulder while retaining that connection.
overview:
From Side Control, the D'Arce becomes available when the opponent's turn or frame opens a path under an armpit and around the neck. Thread the choking arm through that opening, connect a figure-four grip on your own upper arm, and bring the trapped shoulder toward the neck as you adjust the finishing angle.

Marce is a named D'Arce-family finish: move close to the opponent's hip and roll or dive onto the shoulder while keeping the head and arm contained. The choking structure remains a head-and-arm connection. It does not use a lapel as a ligature. It can be practiced in gi and no-gi, and is more commonly taught in no-gi.

The same family is taught from front headlock and half-guard exchanges. This entry's canonical start remains Side Control/Top; the alternative origins shown in companion lessons do not add graph origins or change this entry's outcome table.

injury_risks.injury: Loss of consciousness from neck compression
injury_risks.recovery_time: Stop training; obtain medical assessment if consciousness is lost

injury_risks.injury: Neck or shoulder strain from forced rotation
injury_risks.recovery_time: Varies with injury; persistent pain requires assessment

safety_considerations.application_speed: Slow, progressive pressure with a clear opportunity to tap
tap_signals: Any distress or loss of responsiveness
release_protocol: Open the figure-four immediately on a tap or distress
Release neck and shoulder pressure before changing position
Stop the drill and check the partner before continuing
training_restrictions: Practice the shoulder roll cooperatively before adding resistance
Do not wrench the neck or force a roll through a trapped shoulder
Keep a clear tap signal available throughout the movement

attacker.name: Darce Choke from Side Control (Attacker)
attacker.description: Thread and finish the D'Arce from Side Control, with a controlled Marce shoulder-roll option.
attacker.overview: Contain the opponent's head and arm before committing to the finish. The choking arm travels under the armpit and around the neck; your other arm closes the figure-four. Keep the trapped shoulder connected as you change angle. For the Marce variation, bring the hips close and roll onto the shoulder without letting the arm escape.
key_principles: Secure the head-and-arm connection before adding pressure
Thread under the armpit and around the neck without forcing the cervical spine
Close the figure-four with your own upper arm and keep the elbows connected
Retain the opponent's shoulder beside the neck as you change angle
Use a controlled shoulder roll for the Marce finish while maintaining hip proximity
Release pressure immediately when the partner taps or shows distress
setup_requirements: Side Control/Top with access to the opponent's head and near upper body
An opening under the armpit and around the neck
The opponent's arm contained beside their head rather than free to withdraw
Enough room to adjust the finishing angle without forcing a trapped joint

execution_steps.description: Follow the opponent's turn or frame from Side Control while keeping the head and shoulder within reach.
Pass the arm under the armpit and around the neck, keeping the opponent's arm inside the head-and-arm loop.
Reach your choking hand to your own opposite upper arm and place the supporting hand to keep the structure closed.
Bring the opponent's shoulder toward the side of the neck while closing unnecessary space in the loop.
Maintain the connection as you adjust your body angle. For Marce, move hip to hip and roll onto the shoulder without pulling the neck through the turn.
Close the elbows and add gradual pressure through the connected head-and-arm structure. Open the grip immediately on the partner's tap or distress.

common_counters.counter: Opponent extracts the trapped arm before the grip closes
common_counters.your_response: Recover Side Control and rebuild the opening without chasing an empty neck grip

common_counters.counter: Opponent frames and creates space during the angle change
common_counters.your_response: Follow the shoulder connection or release the attempt and stabilize Side Control

common_counters.counter: Opponent disrupts the roll and reverses the exchange
common_counters.your_response: Release the neck as the connection fails and establish defensive frames from the resulting guard position

common_errors.consequence: The shoulder cannot complete the head-and-arm structure
common_errors.correction: Contain the arm beside the neck before closing the grip

common_errors.consequence: The arms fatigue while the opponent can recover posture
common_errors.correction: Adjust the shoulder and figure-four connection before adding pressure

common_errors.error: Treating Marce as a lapel choke
common_errors.consequence: The grip sequence no longer matches the named variation
common_errors.correction: Use the D'Arce arm thread and shoulder-roll finish in either ruleset

common_errors.error: Rolling while the hip connection is loose
common_errors.consequence: The opponent can withdraw the trapped arm or reverse the exchange
common_errors.correction: Bring the hips close and preserve the loop through a slow roll

common_errors.error: Forcing the head through the finishing angle
common_errors.consequence: The action loads the neck instead of improving the choke structure
common_errors.correction: Reduce pressure, correct the angle, and reset if the connection is unavailable

training_progressions.description: With a cooperative partner, find the armpit-to-neck channel from Side Control and close the figure-four without pressure.
Practice preserving the trapped shoulder as the partner slowly changes their frame and posture; reset when the arm escapes.
Move hip to hip and rehearse the shoulder roll slowly with no finishing pressure, keeping the neck and shoulder free of forced rotation.
Alternate the standard angle and Marce option against light positional resistance, adding pressure only after agreement and releasing on the first signal.

flashcards.question: What structure defines the D'Arce from Side Control?
flashcards.answer: The choking arm passes under the armpit and around the neck, trapping an arm inside a figure-four head-and-arm loop.

trap: Pull head without trapping an arm

flashcards.question: What makes the Marce a named D'Arce variation?
flashcards.answer: The attacker keeps the D'Arce connection while moving hip to hip and rolling onto the shoulder to finish.
flashcards.answer_line: D'Arce grip with a shoulder roll

trap: Any choke finished from the back

flashcards.question: In which rulesets can the Marce variation exist?
flashcards.answer: Its arm-and-shoulder mechanics can be used with or without a gi. It is more commonly taught in no-gi and does not depend on a lapel grip.

flashcards.question: What must remain connected during the Marce roll?
flashcards.answer: Keep the head and trapped arm inside the loop, maintain shoulder containment, and keep the hips close while rotating onto the shoulder.

plausible: Loose hips with a hard neck pull

flashcards.question: What should you do if the arm slips out?
flashcards.answer: Release the failed choke structure and recover positional control. A neck-only grip is not the same attempt.

plausible: Pull the neck to replace the arm
trap: Force the finish through the escape

defender.name: Darce Choke from Side Control (Defender)
defender.description: Recognize the D'Arce thread and protect the head-and-arm connection before the standard or Marce finish closes.
defender.overview: Respond as the arm threads under your armpit toward the neck. Keep room around the trapped shoulder and address the connecting grip before the attacker changes angle. A shoulder roll does not make a secured choke harmless; use the tap if pressure closes before you can restore space.
key_principles: Recognize the under-armpit thread before the figure-four closes
Preserve space around the trapped shoulder and neck
Address the connecting grip before attempting a large positional movement
Follow the changing angle without forcing the neck against the grip
Recover guard or frames only after the choke connection is disrupted
Tap early when the structure is secured and pressure increases
recognition_cues: An arm travels beneath your armpit toward the far side of your neck
The attacker reaches toward their own upper arm to close a figure-four
Your trapped shoulder is drawn toward the side of your neck
The attacker brings their hips close and drops toward a shoulder-roll angle

defensive_options.action: Block the threading arm and recover space around your shoulder
defensive_options.when_to_use: Before the figure-four connection is complete
defensive_options.if_successful: The choke attempt ends while the attacker remains in Side Control/Top
defensive_options.risk: Waiting until the shoulder is compressed leaves less room to move

defensive_options.action: Address the connecting grip while recovering your trapped arm
defensive_options.when_to_use: The attacker is closing the grip but the arm can still be withdrawn
defensive_options.if_successful: The head-and-arm loop opens and positional defense can resume
defensive_options.risk: Pulling the neck against an already secured loop can worsen pressure

defensive_options.action: Use the disrupted rolling exchange to come on top after freeing the neck
defensive_options.when_to_use: The Marce roll loses its head-and-arm connection
defensive_options.if_successful: The attacker lands in Half Guard/Bottom and you recover the top side
defensive_options.risk: Attempting a reversal before the neck is free can tighten the choke

escape_paths: Deny the early thread or extract the trapped arm, then rebuild Side Control frames
Disrupt the grip before the roll and recover guard or the top side as the actual exchange permits

favorable_outcomes.how: Remove the submission connection; this table records the attacker's remaining top position, after which normal Side Control defense resumes
Free the head-and-arm connection during a failed roll and reverse the exchange, leaving the attacker on the bottom side of Half Guard

common_errors.error: Ignoring the arm thread while trying to bridge
common_errors.consequence: The attacker can close the figure-four around the moving head and shoulder
common_errors.correction: Address the choke connection before continuing the positional escape

common_errors.error: Assuming a rolling finish requires a lapel
common_errors.consequence: The defender misses the Marce head-and-arm threat in either ruleset
common_errors.correction: Recognize the D'Arce grip and shoulder-roll angle

common_errors.error: Forcing a turn after pressure has closed
common_errors.consequence: The trapped head and shoulder can take more load
common_errors.correction: Tap when the structure is secured rather than forcing movement through it

flashcards.question: What is the earliest D'Arce warning from Side Control?
flashcards.answer: An arm threads under your armpit toward the neck while your shoulder is drawn inward. Respond before the figure-four closes.

plausible: A hand reaches for a lapel

flashcards.question: What changes when the attacker uses the Marce finish?
flashcards.answer: The attacker moves close to the hip and rolls onto the shoulder while keeping the same head-and-arm connection. The grip still needs to be addressed.
flashcards.answer_line: Shoulder roll keeps the D'Arce grip

plausible: The choke becomes a lapel wrap
trap: The roll alone frees the neck

flashcards.question: When should you resume a positional escape?
flashcards.answer: After the head-and-arm connection is disrupted and the neck has space. If it remains secured under pressure, tap instead of forcing the escape.

trap: Keep moving through a secured choke

training_progressions.description: The partner alternates ordinary Side Control grips with a slow D'Arce thread; identify the attempt before the figure-four closes.
Use a cooperative open grip to rehearse preserving shoulder space and withdrawing the trapped arm, resetting before pressure is applied.
Rehearse a slow shoulder roll without squeeze, identifying when the connection remains intact and when it breaks; practice a clear tap and immediate release.

variations_and_setups.description: Use the opening made by a turn or frame to thread under the armpit and around the neck, connect the figure-four, and adjust your angle while containing the head and arm.
variations_and_setups.when_to_use: A Side Control exchange exposes the armpit-to-neck channel

variations_and_setups.description: Keep the D'Arce head-and-arm connection, move hip to hip, and roll onto the shoulder to finish with the grip close to your torso and the elbows closing.
variations_and_setups.when_to_use: The shoulder-roll angle is available without losing the trapped arm; usable in gi and more common in no-gi

variations_and_setups.description: Follow an opponent turning toward you while keeping their shoulder and head contained, then thread the choking arm through the available opening.
variations_and_setups.when_to_use: The opponent turns toward the passer during Side Control recovery
